QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_45

question.text: Mr. Ramesh Iyer (CFO of a Cat III AIF) is structuring incentive fee crystallisation. Which frequency is MOST COMMON for Cat III open-ended AIFs in India?

answer.text: Monthly, quarterly or annual crystallisation with payment typically at period-end (sometimes deferred to the end of fund term for close-ended)
Crystallisation only on full fund liquidation
Only on investor redemption with no periodic crystallisation

explanation.text: The Logic: For open-ended Cat III AIFs, the prevailing industry practice is to accrue incentive fees in the NAV on an ongoing basis (so subscriptions and redemptions occur at a fair NAV) and crystallise them on a periodic basis — typically monthly, quarterly, or annually — with payment at the end of the crystallisation period. Close-ended Cat III structures often defer the payment of crystallised incentive fees to the end of the fund term. Daily crystallisation is operationally impractical for typical Cat III funds; crystallising only on full liquidation or only on individual redemption is associated with closed-ended/Cat I-II-style structures rather than open-ended Cat III. The Trap: A is operationally impractical for an open-ended NAV-based fund. C reflects a closed-end/Cat I/II crystallisation pattern, not open-ended Cat III. D omits the periodic crystallisation that is standard practice for open-ended funds. Note: The cited NISM Series XIX-E workbook pages (125, 144, 152) support open-ended redemption intervals, regular incentive-fee payment for open-ended funds, and the daily-accrual/end-of-term-payment concept in certain funds, but do not explicitly state that monthly/quarterly/annual crystallisation is the most common Cat III practice. The "most common" framing above is general industry practice rather than a workbook-page citation.
